AI agents find roles, tailor your resume and cover letter to each posting, track applications on a board, and draft follow-ups automatically. 150,000+ apps have been built this way. It starts free.


A job search is really four jobs at once: finding roles, tailoring your resume and cover letter to each one, tracking where every application stands, and remembering to follow up. Most people run all four out of browser tabs and a messy spreadsheet, and applications fall through the cracks.


There is a better shape. You describe what you want to happen, and an AI builds a personal job-search **app** that does the repetitive parts for you. The agents do the tailoring. The board does the tracking. The automations do the chasing. You do the deciding.

## What can AI agents actually do for a job search?


AI agents handle the repetitive, high-volume parts of a job search so you can focus on conversations and decisions. In[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fai-job-search) , agents tailor your resume to each posting, draft a cover letter in seconds, organize roles on a tracker you can sort and filter, and trigger follow-up reminders automatically. They run on built-in tools, including web search and file analysis, and draw on persistent memory so every application stays consistent with your real experience.


The difference from a chat tool is permanence. A chat window forgets you between sessions. A Taskade Genesis workspace remembers your accomplishments, holds every application in a live database, and keeps working in the background.


Here is the whole search as one connected system rather than four disconnected tasks:


## How do AI agents tailor my resume and cover letter?


You hand an agent two things, your accomplishments and the job description, and ask it to rewrite each line to match the role. The[agent](https://www.taskade.com/agents) reads the posting, finds the skills the employer is asking for, and rewrites your experience to mirror that language while keeping it honest. Because the workspace remembers your real history, the rewrites stay grounded in what you have actually done.


The official[help guide for custom job-search agents](https://www.taskade.com/learn/agents/custom-agents) walks through the same idea step by step: create a resume agent, train it on the job description as a knowledge source, paste your accomplishments into a project, then ask the agent to rewrite each bullet to fit the role and even generate likely interview questions.


Here is how that conversation actually flows:


What you get from a single agent chat, end to end:


You ask The agent does


"Where can this resume be sharper?" Flags weak or vague bullets to refine


"Rewrite my experience for this posting" Matches your bullets to the job's language


"Draft a cover letter for this company" Produces a tailored, ready-to-edit draft


"What will they ask in the interview?" Generates likely questions and answers


"Summarize my fit in two sentences" Writes a tight pitch for outreach


Every rewrite is yours to edit. The agent accelerates the draft. You keep the judgment.


## How do I track every application without a spreadsheet?


You track applications in a real database with[multiple project views](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/genesis/projects) , not a static sheet. A **Board** view shows each role as a card moving through Applied, Interviewing, Offer, and Closed. A **Table** view holds company, salary, contact, and the next step. A **Calendar** view puts interviews and deadlines on dates. Because it is a living app, an AI agent can read the tracker and act on it, something a spreadsheet can never do.


The views each answer a different question about your search:


View Answers the question


**Board** What stage is each role at?


**Table** What is the salary, contact, and next step?


**Calendar** When is each interview or deadline?


**List** What do I need to do today?


**Gantt** How does my whole search timeline look?


**Mind Map** How do these roles and referrals connect?


**Org Chart** Who reports to whom at this company?


Timeline scrolling lives inside the Gantt view, so you can zoom your whole pipeline across weeks without leaving the app.


## What do most AI job search tools miss?


Most AI job search tools do one slice of the search and stop there. They **track** , OR they **tailor** , OR they **auto-apply** . So you end up renting three or four of them at once. Resume tools like Teal and Jobscan optimize one resume against one posting. Auto-apply agents like LoopCV, Simplify, and Sonara fire applications at job boards on your behalf. Each is good at its slice. None of them give you one app you own that does all four jobs and remembers everything.


That is the gap. The point tools are *features* ; a job search needs a *system* .[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fai-job-search) builds the whole command center from one prompt, agents that find roles and tailor each application, a Board that tracks them, and reliable automation workflows that chase follow-ups, inside a single workspace you keep, instead of five logins you rent.


These tools genuinely earn their place, and it is worth being clear about what each does best:

If you only need to beat an ATS on a single resume, Jobscan is excellent. If you want a clean tracker with a great resume builder, Teal is a pleasure. If your bottleneck is sheer application volume, an auto-apply agent saves real hours. The honest trade-off: stitch those three together and you are paying for and logging into three products that do not talk to each other, and you own none of the data inside them.

The advantage is not "more features." It is that everything shares one memory. Your tracker, your tailored resumes, and your follow-up automations all read from the same workspace. So the agent that drafts a follow-up already knows which role it is for, what you applied with, and when. Five disconnected subscriptions can never do that, because the data lives in five places you do not own.

## How does AI automate follow-ups so applications don't go cold?


Reliable, durable automation workflows watch your tracker and chase follow-ups for you. When a card sits in "Applied" past a set number of days, the workflow drafts a follow-up message and reminds you to send it. So no application quietly dies. With[100+ bidirectional integrations](https://www.taskade.com/automate) , the workflow can pull a calendar event in and push a drafted email out. Triggers pull events in; actions push data out.


A typical follow-up automation, in plain English:


```text
WHEN  a role has sat in "Applied" for 4 days
AND   no interview is scheduled
DO    draft a polite follow-up message
→ remind me to review and send
→ if still no reply after 7 more days, nudge again


```


You stay in control of every send. The automation only handles the timing and the memory, the two things humans forget under pressure.


## Can a team of agents run the whole search together?


Yes. In **orchestration mode** , several AI agents collaborate like a hiring-search team working for you. One researches and shortlists roles, one rewrites your resume per posting, one drafts outreach and cover letters, and one preps interview questions. They hand work off to each other and route across frontier models from top AI labs. So each task runs on a capable model without you picking one.


This is the[Workspace DNA](https://www.taskade.com/agents) loop applied to your career: **Memory** (your tracked experience and applications) feeds **Intelligence** (the agents), which triggers **Execution** (the follow-up automations), which records new results back into Memory. Each application makes the next one faster.
